paragraphs.text: DSPi turns a Raspberry Pi Pico into a remarkably capable audio processor: equalisation, crossovers, upmixing, loudness compensation and more, applied live to whatever you play.
Setup is short and has one job: getting the DSPi firmware onto your Pico. Once it is running, everything else is set up in the app as you need it.
This app cannot install firmware: use uConsole for DSPi on macOS, Windows or Linux. Once the firmware is running, everything else is set up in the app as you need it.

rows.text: Connect your Pico and install the DSPi firmware, right here.
The board restarts and the app confirms the install worked.
Install the DSPi firmware on your Pico there, then connect it here.
Outputs, wiring and audio are then yours to shape in the console.

paragraphs.text: DSPi turns a Raspberry Pi Pico into a remarkably capable audio processor: equalisation, crossovers, upmixing, loudness compensation and more, applied live to whatever you play.
Setup takes a minute: the DSPi firmware on your Pico, then which output drives what. Both can wait, and the Overview reminds you of what is left.

rows.text: Equalise, cross over, delay and route every output, live as you play.
Measure with a microphone and let auto-tune align crossovers, delays and phase.
Ask an AI agent to make changes for you; by default the app asks you before anything risky.
Already running DSPi firmware? Just plug it in: the next step sees it.
No DSPi yet? Try the demo, a simulated DSPi with every page to explore.

headers.title: Prepare your Pico
headers.blurb: In this step, we are going to install the DSPi firmware on your Pico-compatible device. Follow the directions below.

headers.title: Your device is ready
headers.blurb: This step installs the DSPi firmware, and your connected device is already running it. There is nothing to do here.

headers.title: Update your firmware
headers.blurb: Your DSPi is already connected, so no buttons need holding: the app can restart it and install the matching firmware in one step.

headers.title: Your firmware is newer
headers.blurb: This Console ships an older firmware than your device is running. Updating the app is usually the better fix, but you can also downgrade the device to match.

headers.title: Installing firmware
headers.blurb: Console ships the firmware it expects, so nothing needs a download. Keep the Pico plugged in until it checks back in.

headers.title: One question first
headers.blurb: The firmware guard has a question about this board's core voltage. Nothing has changed yet.

headers.title: Nothing was written
headers.blurb: The update was cancelled after the board had already restarted.

headers.title: Firmware written
headers.blurb: The firmware went to the board, but whether it took could not be confirmed. The card below says why.

headers.title: Your device has been prepared
headers.blurb: The device has successfully restarted and DSPi Firmware is correctly installed.

headers.title: Something needs attention
headers.blurb: This is almost always fixable. Follow the card below, then try again - nothing has been lost.

cards.title: Waiting for your Pico
cards.text: Hold the BOOTSEL button while connecting your Pico-compatible device[[if macos: to your computer]]. Once detected, it will appear here.

cards.title: Looking for your Pico
cards.text: Waiting for it to appear in bootloader mode. If nothing happens after a few seconds, unplug it, hold BOOTSEL, and plug it back in.

cards.title: {chip} found
cards.text: The board is in bootloader mode. Waiting for its {volume} drive to mount - this usually takes a second or two.

cards.title: {chip} ready
cards.text: The device is now in bootloader mode and ready to receive firmware.

cards.title: Writing firmware
cards.text: Near the end the board restarts itself and its drive disappears. That is normal - do not unplug it.

cards.title: Firmware written
cards.text: The board is restarting with its new firmware. This can take up to half a minute; leave it plugged in.

cards.title: Firmware {version} installed
cards.text: That was the whole job. Continue to finish setup.

cards.title: Firmware {bundled_version} already installed
cards.text: Your DSPi is running the firmware this Console ships, so there is nothing to install. Continue to finish setup.

cards.title: Firmware update available
cards.text: Your DSPi is running firmware {device_version}; this Console pairs with {bundled_version}. The device will restart into bootloader mode and come back updated. Audio stops until it finishes.

cards.title: This would be a downgrade
cards.text: Your DSPi is running firmware {device_version}, which is newer than this Console expects ({bundled_version}). A newer Console is the better fix, but you can downgrade the device to match this one.

cards.title: Checking
cards.text: Looking at the firmware and the board. Nothing has changed yet.

cards.title: Restarting into bootloader mode
cards.text: Waiting for the board's drive to appear.

paragraphs.text: Your Pico is running the DSPi firmware, and the console is ready whenever it is plugged in. A few places worth knowing about:
The console is ready whenever your DSPi is connected. A few places worth knowing about:

rows.text: Choose which outputs your build uses, and the pins that carry them, in Settings under [[hardware_page]].
Pick the DSPi as the output device in [[sound_settings]] to hear [[if macos:your computer]][[if not_macos:audio]] through it.
Connect the DSPi over USB to hear audio through it.
[[if desktop:Click an input or output in the sidebar]][[if mobile:Tap an input or output]] to edit its filters.
Help holds release notes and links, and this wizard can be run again.

paragraphs.text: The console is ready whenever your DSPi is plugged in. A few places worth knowing about:

rows.text: Choose which outputs your build uses, and the pins that carry them, in Settings under [[hardware_page]].
Pick the DSPi as the output device in [[sound_settings]] to hear audio through it; Check Sound Output tells you whether it already is.
The Overview keeps a short list of what is left to set up: speakers, routing, crossovers, a measurement and a save.
Choose a card on the Overview, or Equaliser in the rail, to edit a channel's filters.
Click an input or output in the sidebar to edit its filters.
The uConsole menu at the top left holds What's New, the help links and this wizard; the command palette[[shortcut:K]] finds any page or command.
Help holds release notes and links, and this wizard can be run again.
